issues.title: Refine creator-managed participant fields from accepted entries
issues.body:
## Context

Research #185 recommends an explicit private participant-field boundary before drawing. See openspec/changes/issue-185-draw-structures/findings.md and code-reconciliation.md. The merged #219 entry book retains local string player keys and explicit pairs; legacy rosters use numeric references, so acceptance must not silently become roster membership.

## Scope

Run a full feature lifecycle to refine and, only after its explicit approvals, implement creator-managed participant-field preparation for one bracket from deliberately selected ACCEPTED entry snapshots. Choose local playing-unit identity, source/field revisions, configuration compatibility, duplicate and manual capacity policy, authority/privacy and correction/withdrawal reconciliation. Preserve member snapshots and provenance without fabricating global player/team IDs or changing existing entry/draft behavior. Obtain an ADR for ownership and persistence/transaction decisions; assess any additive migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- Approved requirements distinguish an entry, a prepared participant field and a future draw, with explicit singles/doubles membership and local unverified identity.
- The creator deliberately prepares a private field from current accepted entries for a compatible bracket; invalid/stale/foreign requests preserve the prior state and do not disclose private data.
- Source revisions, saved member/selection snapshots and field revisions have an explicit consistency contract, including correction, withdrawal and draft-edit reconciliation.
- Existing entry acceptance does not gain automatic synchronization side effects; no string keys are cast/hashed into legacy numeric roster IDs.
- Architecture, migration, privacy/retention and backward-compatibility decisions are reviewed before implementation; checks trace all scenarios and include local authenticated UAT.

## Exclusions

No draw generator, seeding/ranking automation, result/standings engine, automatic capacity admission, federation integration, verified player directory, frontend stack or public participant publication. Selecting a later format and its rule edition remains separate work.

Depends on completed #219. The research recommendation is not implementation approval; this follow-up must pass its own full lifecycle.
